hero.label: 01 — Your room
hero.title: Your room, in 3D. *Before you buy a thing.*
hero.lead: Photograph your room, set a budget, and see it furnished with real pieces. Same walls, same light.
hero.desktopNote: Photographing a room needs a phone camera. On a computer, upload the photos or build the room from its dimensions.
hero.qrBody: Scan this and the capture flow opens on your phone, signed into the same account.

steps.label: 02 — How it works
steps.title: Three steps, *about four minutes.*
steps.lead: No measuring tape, no floor plan, no designer appointment.

items.title: Photograph the room
items.body: Six or seven photos, turning on the spot. The app names each wall in turn and records which way the phone was facing, so nothing gets guessed later.

items.title: Choose a style and a budget
items.body: Pick the look, then set what you are willing to spend. The furniture list is costed against that number and never quietly goes over it.

items.title: See it in the room
items.body: Your own photographs come back restyled — same walls, same windows, same daylight. Then point the phone at the room and look around inside it.

catalog.label: 03 — Catalog
catalog.title: Furniture in *real 3D*, not flat photographs.
catalog.lead: Rotate a piece, look underneath it, then drop it into your own room and see whether it actually fits.
catalog.hint: Every piece is a real 3D model

ai.label: 04 — The suggestion
ai.title: Photographs in. *A costed room out.*
ai.lead: The room is read first — dimensions, windows, doors, radiators, where the daylight comes from — and the design is built around what cannot move.

outputs.title: Furniture, priced
outputs.body: Every piece with a realistic market price, a quantity and a place in the room — and a total measured against your budget.

outputs.title: Light, by direction
outputs.body: Where the daylight falls, what to add, and at what colour temperature. The renders keep your real window where it is.

outputs.title: Sockets and electrics
outputs.body: What needs a socket, what needs moving, and what the lamp on the far wall will cost you in cable.

live.label: 05 — See by yourself
live.title: Stand in the room *you have not bought yet.*
live.lead: Go back to where you took the photographs, face the same way, and press Start. The phone shows your real room, live, in the new design — turn around and the design turns with you.

steps.title: Return to the spot
steps.body: The first photo you took is the anchor. The app knows which way you were facing.

steps.title: Line up with the guide
steps.body: A ghost of that photo and a heading tape help you match it. Within about ten degrees, Start unlocks.

steps.title: Press Start and look around
steps.body: Turn the phone and the restyled room turns with it. Tilt up and you see the ceiling. Hold to see the room as it is now.

live.mobileOnly: Runs on the phone — it needs the camera and the compass. On a computer we show you a QR code instead.

business.label: 06 — For business
business.title: Your whole catalog, in 3D, *in your customer's own room.*
business.lead: Every furniture brand and store gets its own dashboard and its own 3D catalog. Upload a product once; customers rotate it, filter it and place it in the room they actually live in.

points.title: Your own dashboard
points.body: Products, prices, stock and tags. Upload in bulk, see which pieces get opened and rotated.

points.title: A 3D catalog, not a PDF
points.body: Each product becomes a model the customer can turn around and stand next to their own sofa.

points.title: Placements, not just views
points.body: You see how often a piece was dropped into a real room — the signal that matters before someone walks in.

points.title: Your branding
points.body: Your logo, your colours, your own catalog page. It reads as your store, not as ours.

items.q: Do I need to measure the room?
items.a: No. The dimensions are estimated from the photographs — door heights, sockets and floorboards give the scale away. You are told how confident that estimate is, and you can correct it in the 3D builder if you want to.

items.q: Are these my walls, or a stock photo of someone else's room?
items.a: Yours. Each render is your own photograph, repainted. The wall positions, the window, the door and the direction the light comes from are all kept exactly where they are.

items.q: Can I actually buy the furniture?
items.a: The list comes with realistic market prices so the budget means something. Where a piece exists in the catalog of a store working with us, it links straight through. The rest is a specification you can take to any shop.

items.q: Does 'See by yourself' work on an iPhone?
items.a: Yes. It asks for the camera and the motion sensors, and iOS requires you to tap to grant that. If the phone is old or offline, it falls back to a 360° panorama built from the renders, which works everywhere.

items.q: What if I do not have a budget in mind?
items.a: Leave it empty. You still get an honest total, priced at the middle of the normal retail range rather than the cheapest thing that could be found.

Your projects are saved to your account so you can come back to them, and you can delete any project — photographs included — at any time. Without an account nothing leaves your device except the one generation you asked for.
